design_notes.what_this_feature_is: The sixth feature of phase 013: adds a plain-markdown pull-request checklist at .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md naming standard/definition_of_done.md as the canonical Definition of Done and projecting its Merge-Done layer (Section 8) into at least eight actionable checkboxes a human reviewer and the PR author both see on every pull request. This is a merge-layer PROJECTION, not a restatement -- it names each check by the standard's own vocabulary and points back to the canonical document, mirroring the aggregate-don't-restate discipline standard/definition_of_done.md Section 1 itself models.
design_notes.c1_c9_scope_verification: Independently re-verified today against the current tree (base_revision) before pinning any content-shape requirement, per the task's explicit instruction to check before writing path-dependent checks. (1) check_c1_frontmatter_schema and check_c8_version_changelog (tools/validate.sh) both sweep only the file set built_shipped_md_set() returns (tools/validate.sh lines 425-456): CONTEXT.md, docs/architecture/*.md, standard/*.md, methodology/*.md, registry/*.md, templates/*.md, tools/*.md (excluding tools/fixtures/), and schema/README.md. That function contains no reference to .github/ anywhere, in either its explicit path list or its `for d in ...` loop, so .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md is NOT a member of the shipped_md set C1 or C8 sweep in default mode; build_payload_md_set() (lines 462-489, used by --payload mode) sweeps only standard/templates/methodology/ecosystem plus tools/*.md and schema/README.md -- likewise no .github/ reference. CONCLUSION: the template requires no NDS.md six-key frontmatter block and is not subject to C8's version/change_log pairing rule; it is plain markdown by design, not merely by choice. (2) check_c9_path_resolution's default-mode sweep set (tools/validate.sh line 2509, c9_default_files) is `shipped_md + docs/guide/index.html` -- the same shipped_md set from (1) plus one HTML file, again with no .github/ member; the --payload-mode sweep (payload_md, line 2486) is likewise shipped_md-derived with no .github/ member. CONCLUSION: no directory-qualified path token this document writes will ever be scanned by check C9 in either mode, so a stray unresolved reference inside this template cannot trip C9 today, regardless of DAG landing order. (3) tools/fixtures_self_test.sh's .github/ references (grep-confirmed at lines 359, 366, and 370 -- three sites, all within the same C14 SHA-pin scratch-probe block: line 359 is the block's own comment, line 366 builds a scratch fixture containing a `./.github/actions/local` string, and line 370 is the actual `vlib_workflows_sha_pinned .github/workflows` invocation against the real tree) are confined entirely to that one probe -- it contains no disk-to-index enumeration guard over .github/*.md and does not sweep this template at all. NET EFFECT: this feature's file rides entirely outside every governed-doc mechanical sweep in the repository today; the file's only mechanical guarantees are its own contract's acceptance tests (existence, checkbox count/content, and the standard/definition_of_done.md self-reference) plus the fact that its own presence must not regress the unrelated sixteen checks (verification below).
design_notes.gate_naming_decision: Even though c1_c9_scope_verification above shows C9 would not, in fact, catch a dangling .github/workflows/release_closeout.yml reference inside this file (no automated check sweeps it), this contract still prescribes the SAME no-forward-path discipline contract 093 applied to its own Section 11 (093's design_notes.banner_phrasing_decision): the release close-out gate is named GENERICALLY, by feature id and phase -- 'the release close-out gate defined by phase 013, feature 097' -- never by directory-qualified path, in the required checklist item. Rationale, independent of C9's blind spot: (a) correctness for its own sake -- a checklist item pointing at a path that may not exist yet at the moment this feature's implementation actually lands is simply wrong prose, whether or not a linter catches it; (b) consistency with the house no-forward-path convention already established twice this phase (093's own banner and Section 11); (c) 097 is a DAG root with no dependency ordering guarantee relative to 096, so the generator cannot assume landing order at implementation time. EXEMPTION (mirrors 093's non_goals precedent): if, at the moment this feature's implementation is verified, .github/workflows/release_closeout.yml is confirmed GIT-TRACKED (`git ls-files --error-unmatch .github/workflows/release_closeout.yml`, not merely present on disk -- an untracked scratch or in-progress file is not a durable guarantee and does not satisfy this exemption), the generator MAY additionally cite the pathful form alongside the generic one in that same checklist line (e.g. 'the release close-out gate (phase 013, feature 097, .github/workflows/release_closeout.yml)') -- never as a REPLACEMENT for the generic phrase, only as a supplement, and only when independently confirmed git-tracked at that moment. The generic phrase is the contracted minimum in all cases; verification below asserts the generic phrase is always present and, separately, that IF any literal '.github/workflows/' substring appears anywhere in the file, every such occurrence resolves to a git-tracked file (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`), not merely a path that happens to exist on disk.
design_notes.checklist_content_spec: Exactly nine `- [ ]` checkbox lines (the plan's F-096 paragraph lists nine concrete items verbatim; nine is both the contracted floor-satisfying count and the ceiling this contract pins, so verification can assert an exact structural count rather than a loose minimum while still meeting the feature-list's own `-ge 8` verbatim acceptance test). Each of the nine covers exactly one topic, checked below by required keyword-set per line rather than exact wording (the generator retains phrasing latitude; the review is discriminating on CONTENT, not on exact prose): (1) tools/validate.sh reports SUMMARY 16 passed / 0 failed across checks C1-C16. (2) tools/fixtures_self_test.sh exits 0. (3) tools/e2e_bootstrap_test.sh exits 0, when this change touches injected payload surfaces. (4) Every governed doc touched pairs a version bump with a change_log entry (check C8's pairing rule, named by concept). (5) Every feature claimed `complete` in this change carries the full C16 chain: an approved contract, a passing QA verdict, and evidence resolving on disk. (6) Evidence files follow the methodology/04_tool_driven_state.md Section 5 shape (exact invocation, captured output, a final EXIT:<code> line). (7) CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section carries an entry for this change. (8) If this change touches release surfaces, the release close-out gate (named per gate_naming_decision) is green. (9) This PR is not self-merged; the release tag remains operator-only. The file additionally opens with one summary line stating its purpose, and a sentence reading, in substance, that the canonical DoD is `standard/definition_of_done.md` and this checklist is its merge-layer projection -- the exact clause the feature-list's acceptance_tests[2] greps for is `standard/definition_of_done.md`, backticked as a path per house convention though this file is not itself NDS-governed.
design_notes.hard_style_rules: No YAML frontmatter block (c1_c9_scope_verification above; the file is not a member of any governed-doc sweep and carries none of NDS.md's six required keys). Every repository-relative path named in the body (standard/definition_of_done.md, tools/validate.sh, tools/fixtures_self_test.sh, tools/e2e_bootstrap_test.sh, methodology/04_tool_driven_state.md, CHANGELOG.md) is backticked, matching house convention even though this file rides outside C9's mechanical enforcement of that convention. No markdown link syntax `[text](path)` anywhere. GitHub renders this file directly as the PR description scaffold on every new pull request against this repository once it exists at this exact path and name (GitHub convention: `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, case- and path-exact, no configuration required) -- the generator MUST NOT rename it to a variant filename (e.g. `pull_request_template.md` or the `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/` multi-template directory form), preserving the exact filename the feature-list's own acceptance_tests[0] asserts.
design_notes.ndebt_040_carve_out: NDEBT-040 (docs/planning/DEBT.md, OPEN, Low) records that a contract's byte-identity guard against .agent/run_state.json is unsatisfiable under live concurrent orchestration, because the orchestrator legitimately appends coordination records to that file between contract approval and QA -- exactly the live situation here, since siblings 094/095/097 are proposed/implementing concurrently and will themselves touch run_state.json. Per NDEBT-040's own prescription ('byte-guards in contracts scope to feature lists only -- the 092 precedent'), this contract's byte-identity verification test below scopes exclusively to .agent/feature_list_013.json content and does NOT assert byte-identity on .agent/run_state.json; run_state's coordination-key churn (updated_at, active_contract_id, circuit_breaker, appended history entries) from concurrent sibling activity is explicitly out of this contract's guard, matching contract 092's and 093's identical carve-out.

import re
text = open('.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md').read()

missing = [name for name, ok in checks if not ok]
assert not missing, f'missing checklist topics: {missing}'

verification.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, subprocess
from pathlib import Path
ANCHOR = "b451b96"
SIBLING_097_ALLOWLIST = {
    ".github/workflows/release_closeout.yml",
    ".github/workflows/release.yml",
    ".github/scripts/release_closeout.py",
}
OWN_FILE = ".github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md"
contract = json.loads(Path(".agent/contracts/096.json").read_text())
own_paths = [f["path"] for f in contract["scope"]["files_create"]] + [f["path"] for f in contract["scope"]["files_modify"]]
workflow_in_own_scope = [p for p in own_paths if p.startswith(".github/workflows/")]
assert not workflow_in_own_scope, f"096's own contracted scope authors a workflow file: {workflow_in_own_scope}"
tracked = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--name-only", ANCHOR, "--", ".github/"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.split()
status = subprocess.run(["git", "status", "--porcelain", "-uall", "--", ".github/"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.splitlines()
untracked = [line[3:] for line in status if line.startswith("??")]
all_deltas = sorted(set(tracked) | set(untracked))
unexplained = [p for p in all_deltas if p != OWN_FILE and p not in SIBLING_097_ALLOWLIST]
assert not unexplained, f"unexplained .github/ delta(s) since anchor, outside 096's own scope and the sibling-097 allowlist: {unexplained}"
stray_workflow = [p for p in all_deltas if p.startswith(".github/workflows/") and p not in SIBLING_097_ALLOWLIST]
assert not stray_workflow, f"unexplained workflow delta: {stray_workflow}"
print(f"PASS .github/ deltas since {ANCHOR} confined to 096's own PR template plus sibling-097-owned paths: {all_deltas}")
PY
